81676.subject: Binance Sets Aside $6.34 Billion to Cover Its Hack
81676.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* [**Binance**](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-it-has-reserved-over-6-34-billion-to-cover-hack-losses)[ reserved $6.34B to cover the hack](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-it-has-reserved-over-6-34-billion-to-cover-hack-losses)

* [**Chainalysis**](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-links-6-4-billion-binance-hack-to-north-korea)[ linked the hack to North Korea](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-links-6-4-billion-binance-hack-to-north-korea)

* [**Aave**](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-reopens-markets-but-keeps-nine-assets-at-zero-ltv)[ reopened with nine assets at zero LTV](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-reopens-markets-but-keeps-nine-assets-at-zero-ltv)

* [**Bitcoin**](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-trades-below-80-000-as-long-liquidations-hit-1-34-billion)[ fell below $80K on $1.34B of liquidations](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-trades-below-80-000-as-long-liquidations-hit-1-34-billion)

* [**Trezor**](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/trezor-urges-cryptobilis-buyers-to-move-funds-after-implant-report)[ told CryptoBilis buyers to move funds](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/trezor-urges-cryptobilis-buyers-to-move-funds-after-implant-report)

Binance says it has [reserved more than $6.34 billion](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-it-has-reserved-over-6-34-billion-to-cover-hack-losses) of company funds to cover Thursday's hack, which it estimates hit about $6.3 billion in assets. About $5 billion of that reserve is already held in the same tokens that were stolen. Co-CEO Richard Teng said the hacked hot wallet held Binance's own funds and that most customer assets sit in cold wallets. He said withdrawals should restart before Sunday, with a full proof-of-reserves report [by Monday, Nov. 2](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-s-teng-sets-monday-reserve-report-deadline-as-withdrawals-stay-paused).

The roughly $3 billion that partners froze sits outside that reserve. Binance counts it separately because a frozen token has not been returned. Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs Binance, posted his own [rough math](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/cz-says-binance-hack-leaves-2-billion-gap-points-to-spacex-shares). In his count, the frozen funds and an emergency fund he puts above $1 billion leave a gap of about $2 billion. He said Binance holds more than $1 billion in SpaceX shares to help fill it. Neither figure has been verified. Binance's own page valued that fund at about $1 billion in bitcoin as of Oct. 13.

DeFi felt some of the shockwaves. Aave froze its markets on Thursday evening, a day after it [raised borrowing limits](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-raises-bitcoin-and-ether-collateral-borrowing-limits-across-v3-and-v4) for bitcoin and ether collateral. It [reopened them today](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-reopens-markets-but-keeps-nine-assets-at-zero-lt

81672.subject: Crypto Biz: Bitcoin’s quantum threat is becoming an economic problem
81672.body:
Crypto Biz Newsletter

Автор: Cointelegraph


Автор: Cointelegraph

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/crypto-biz-bitcoins-quantum-threat-becoming-economic-problem-awprc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BsBz0i0YaRpexD%2FAN05%2BBtg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1eI6NDP_Ru5cw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvv4m3fn~3r-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvv4m3fn-3r
  
The debate over quantum computing has raised serious questions about Bitcoin’s long-term security, but the economic consequences could emerge long before the technology seriously threatens the network. Muneeb Ali, founder of Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, believes quantum computing risks are already discouraging institutional investment, even as US spot Bitcoin ETFs have amassed more than $104 billion in net assets, according to BitBo data. He warns that BTC has only a few years to prepare for the transition to quantum-resistant security, a process that could take years given the network’s history of slow and contentious upgrades. For institutional investors drawn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement, doubts about its long-term security could complicate the investment case.  This week’s Crypto Biz explores the quantum threat, alongside new developments surrounding Ripple, VanEck and European stablecoin adoption.  Quantum computing fears are already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says Bitcoin could face a more serious security challenge if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum resistance by 2028, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network’s lengthy upgrade process leaves little room for delays. Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Ali said Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap for becoming quantum-resistant, with meaningful progress required by 2028. He cited 2030 as the target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant security, based on guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, though advances in artificial intelligence could bring that deadline forward. Even if developers agree on how to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks, implementing the changes could take years. Holders would then need time to move their Bitcoin to quantum-resistant addresses. Although some industry participants dispute the urgency of the threat, Ali argued that uncertainty alone could undermine investor confidence. He also warned that a quantum breakthrough capable of compromising Bitcoin would have consequences for the broader cryptocurrency market.
